title: Graph collision

problem.name: Graph collision
problem.statement_latex:
A graph $G=([n],E)$ is known in advance; oracle bits $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ mark vertices. Decide whether $\exists\{u,v\}\in E$ with $x_u=x_v=1$, and find such an edge. The graph structure is free input, whereas marks are queried.
Complexity counts queries to the mark bits; the known graph is available independently of this oracle.
problem.statement_text: A graph $G=([n],E)$ is known in advance; oracle bits $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ mark vertices. Decide whether $\exists\{u,v\}\in E$ with $x_u=x_v=1$, and find such an edge. The graph structure is free input, whereas marks are queried. Complexity counts queries to the mark bits; the known graph is available independently of this oracle.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(n^{11/17})$ queries, Cornelissen et al.; $O(\sqrt n\,\alpha(G)^{1/6})$ for the independence-number refinement.
quantum.headline_text: $\widetilde O(n^{11/17})$ queries, Cornelissen et al.; $O(\sqrt n\,\alpha(G)^{1/6})$ for the independence-number refinement.
quantum.details_latex: The November 2026 algorithm splits high- and low-degree neighborhoods and combines quantum search with sampled graph structure. Here $\alpha(G)$ is the independence number. The earlier general quantum-walk construction uses $O(n^{2/3})$ queries. The quantum lower bound is $\Omega(\sqrt{n\log n})$ over an appropriate family of known graphs.
quantum.details_text: The November 2026 algorithm splits high- and low-degree neighborhoods and combines quantum search with sampled graph structure. Here $\alpha(G)$ is the independence number. classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(n)$ mark queries, exhaustive reading and randomized search.
classical.headline_text: $\Theta(n)$ mark queries, exhaustive reading and randomized search.
classical.details_latex: Reading all marks permits direct checking of the known edge set. A star with its center marked embeds an unstructured search over the other marks, giving the linear classical lower bound. Graph preprocessing and checking a stored edge relation have additional time costs outside the mark-query measure.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial: $n\to\widetilde O(n^{11/17})$ in the worst case. The algorithms use quantum search, quantum walks and graph structure.
strength.description_text: Polynomial: $n\to\widetilde O(n^{11/17})$ in the worst case. The algorithms use quantum search, quantum walks and graph structure.

evidence.description_latex: The quantum upper bound and classical lower bound give a rigorous query separation; the strongest cited bound is a November 2026 preprint.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant coherent processing is required. The $O(n^{2/3})$ walk uses roughly $\widetilde O(n^{2/3})$ coherent bits for stored labels and marks. The $11/17$ query exponent has its own implementation-dependent workspace costs.
